We show that double-horizon BHs have a double light ring in the potential, and for a certain value $Ω/χ^2=0.01,$ the QNMs are similar to the GR case since the horizon is Schwarzschild-like. We also tested the correspondence between the QNMs and the graybody factor, and our results still hold with an error far below $1\%$. Our results also conclude that the higher the frequency, the bigger the cross-section area. For the optical observables, we observe that the opposite sign of $Ω$ leads to distinct behavior of the BH's photon sphere and shadow radius. The Sagittarius A* shadow radius upper bound from the Event Horizon Telescope observation in the $2σ$ and $1σ$ significance set the upper limit of the quantum parameter $Ω$ to $Ω/χ^2 \lesssim 0.3649$ and $Ω/χ^2 \lesssim 0.0105$, respectively.

title: Gauging background isometries of the ILST null string
summary: We present a general gauging of a subalgebra, $\mathfrak h$, of the isometries $\mathfrak g$ of the background geometry for the ILST string (e-Print: hep-th/9307108 [hep-th]). We discuss which of the isometries in $\mathfrak g$ survive the gauging as symmetries. The gauged symmetry does not in general involve transformations of the vector density V. There is thus a corresponding contraction of the algebra of constraints as compared to the flat background and it no longer represent the full Carroll-Weyl algebra. This algebra of constraints is derived and discussed, partly in an appendix. The gauging of isometries sets the stage for a reduction, or quotient construction, leading to a new null string on the space of orbits of the gauge group. We illustrate this by deriving the ILST string in $AdS$ background as a quotient of a model in SO(d,2) background by a SO(d,1) isometry, in group space

title: Weight-space programming and mechanistic interpretability for model editing in particle physics
summary: We demonstrate that weight-space programming and edits guided by sparse autoencoders can remove unwanted aspects of a particle-physics foundation model through direct edits to its weights. In a foundation model trained on jets, we observe that adding a single soft neutral particle causes large changes in jet classification, violating infrared safety. We locate the responsible attention heads with mechanistic analysis and trace the flaw's origin to pretraining on datasets with different reconstruction thresholds. We then propose two targeted approaches to repair the flaw: by removing three latent directions identified with sparse autoencoders, and by letting language-model agents edit the weights directly, without gradients and with only 50 queries to the model. Both their edits individually remove almost the entire flaw and leave the rest of the model's response nearly unchanged. Compared to fine-tuning, both methods change far fewer parameters. Although built only on $W$ and QCD jets, the edits carry over to all signal classes, the pretrained generator, and a newly trained regression head.

title: Precise Interstellar Extinction Estimates for Nearly Ten Million Stars Based on Multiple Spectroscopic Surveys
comment: Accepted for publication in Research in Astronomy and Astrophysics (RAA). 22 pages, 9 figures, 2 tables
summary: Accurate interstellar extinction estimates are vital for revealing the intrinsic physical properties of stars and the dynamic structure of the Milky Way. Based on multiple optical and near-infrared spectroscopic surveys, including LAMOST, APOGEE, GALAH, GaiaESO, SEGUE, and DESI, we use MLPs and polynomial regressions to calibrate giants and dwarfs separately onto the APOGEE parameter scale, constructing a combined spectroscopic catalog of nearly ten million stars with calibrated stellar atmospheric parameters. This catalog not only provides a robust dataset for our extinction measurements, but also serves as a reference sample for estimating stellar parameters from photometric surveys. Both cross-survey comparisons and external comparisons with high-resolution spectroscopic benchmarks show good agreement in the calibrated parameters. By applying the star-pair method to this extensive sample, we obtain precise extinction estimates. Incorporating distance information, we characterize the spatial distribution of extinction covering over 33,000 square degrees of the sky. Comparisons with existing literature demonstrate that our extinction estimates achieve an exceptional precision of 0.019-0.022 mag. The value-added catalog and open-source Python pipeline for line-of-sight extinction released in this work will provide robust support for future Galactic structure studies and photometric calibrations.

title: Cosmological Correlators with Triple Massive Exchanges
summary: Among all tree-level contributions to the primordial bispectrum, the triple exchange of massive scalars is the most challenging. In this paper we present an analytical formula for this bispectrum in the form of a double series, which allows the three exchanged fields to have different masses and converges throughout the whole physical region. We obtain it by expanding the mixed propagator with the softest momentum, so that the triple exchange becomes a sum of integrals over two mixed propagators. Each of these integrals satisfies a differential equation and is fixed by its value at equal momentum. We further show that the squeezed limit follows directly from this formula and takes a simple and compact form.

title: The role of gas on the collisional runaway path to supermassive black hole seeds
summary: The origin of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) remains unclear, despite observational evidence for their rapid formation in the early Universe, as evidenced by active galactic nuclei (AGN) at high redshift. We perform a series of coupled N-body and SPH simulations using the AMUSE framework, with the stellar and gaseous components interacting gravitationally via the BRIDGE method. We use 12 initial condition models with equal-mass stars following Plummer distributions, with total masses ranging from $10^3$ to $5 \times 10^5~M_{\odot}$, virial radii from $0.005$ to $0.1$ pc, and stellar masses of $1$, $10$ and $50$ $M_{\odot}$. We find that in most of our simulations, higher gas fractions lead to the formation of more massive black hole, as the core collapses earlier, triggering collisions through gas--star interactions. Our results show increases in BH mass of $\sim 8\%$ for low gas fractions, to $\sim 44\%$ at 20\% gas fraction. The core collapse time is also shortened, with the strongest reduction at $20\%$ gas fraction ($\sim 27\%$). Although our simulations do not fully resolve this effect, gas--star interactions are the principal mechanism driving the enhancement in BH formation efficiency, in the absence of other dissipation mechanisms.

title: The $a$-function in fractional dimensions
summary: We consider the $β$-functions for both scalar, and supersymmetric chiral scalar, field theories with a general $n$th-order self-interaction, in their critical dimensions, which are in general non-integer. We perform a full computation up to fourth order in the coupling in the supersymmetric case, and a partial one in the scalar case. We then demonstrate the existence of an $a$-function, related to the $β$-functions by a gradient flow with a positive-definite metric, through fourth order in the coupling in the supersymmetric case; and show that all our fourth-order results in the scalar case are consistent with a similar property holding there too.

title: Electronic Wichmann-Kroll correction to the energy levels of muonic hydrogen-like atoms
summary: Using modern multiloop calculation methods, we obtain correction to energy levels of muonic hydrogen-like atoms due to the leading-order ($\proptoα(Zα)^3$) Wichmann-Kroll electronic potential. Our result is expressed in terms of generalized polylogarithms. As a byproduct, we also obtain the Wichmann-Kroll potential in momentum space in terms of the same functions.

title: Diffusing the assumptions: towards realistic LISA stochastic component separation with physics-aware simulation-based inference
summary: Simultaneous global-fit inference of the numerous sources observed by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) depends on accurate modeling of its stochastic components: instrumental noise, the Galactic foreground, and astrophysical or stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds (SGWB). Realistic features such as non-Gaussian transients and data gaps challenge traditional likelihood-based pipelines, creating an opportunity for simulation-based inference (SBI) to augment traditional analyses. Here, we present an SBI framework for LISA stochastic component separation built on the Simformer, a transformer trained with diffusion or flow matching that ingests the full time-delay interferometry cross-spectral matrix via a physics-aware embedding. We progressively relax standard simplifying assumptions on simulated 11.6-day datasets containing a loud foreground and a faint power-law SGWB. With unequal arms and per-link noise freedom, the networks match 17-dimensional MCMC posteriors after importance reweighting; full cross-spectra constrain each link's optical metrology noise amplitude to $1\%$. When marginalizing over glitches or massive black hole binary transients, estimation errors remain flat up to transient signal-to-noise ratios of several hundred, whereas ignoring them severely biases likelihood fits. Under time-varying spline noise levels, realistic glitch rates, and gaps up to one day long, posterior coverage remains nominal or conservative across $\sim 10^4$ simulations. We test coverage in the local neighborhood of a given observation by introducing a novel importance-weighted localized simulation-based calibration test. We find flow matching slightly better calibrated than diffusion in simpler regimes and observe modest gains from physics-aware template inputs. Finally, we outline how these networks can initialize the noise and stochastic blocks of a LISA global fit.

title: Ohmic warm inflation
summary: We show that Warm Little Inflation is anomalous, lacks a suitable inflaton potential, and cannot sustain the thermal bath, as the quasi-static approximation over-estimated the dissipated power. To address these issues, we propose a new friction mechanism and new anomaly-free models based on one fermion charged under a U(1) gauge group in one extra dimension. The four-dimensional lattice version is a ring of $N$ U(1) groups with one fermion at each site, reducing to an anomaly-free version of the warm little inflaton model for $N=2$. The inflaton is a Wilson line, protected for $N\ge5$. Large $N$ allows a suitable monodromy inflaton potential. In the continuum limit, $N\to\infty$, the inflaton velocity becomes a five-dimensional electric field and friction becomes Ohmic dissipation, which seems able to sustain warm inflation compatibly with observations.

title: Broad-line ambiguity in IC 1495
comment: 19 pages, 10 figures, 14 tables, including appendices, submitted to MNRAS
summary: Published analyses disagree on whether the 2004 6dFGS spectrum of IC 1495, a barred Seyfert galaxy in the 2MIG isolated-galaxy catalogue, contains broad H-alpha. Among six H-alpha+[N II] models with free narrow-line kinematics, the BIC-preferred fit includes broad H-alpha with intrinsic FWHM ~2000 km/s. However, adding broad H-alpha worsens the BIC when H-alpha and [N II] share two narrow kinematic components. Broad H-alpha is not detected in the 2004 spectrum under the adopted criterion. Injection-recovery simulations of a reference broad component (FWHM ~1930 km/s; broad-to-narrow H-alpha flux ratio 0.82) yield recovery fractions of 27-35% in baseline simulations and 11-55% across the grid. At 1.5 times this flux ratio, baseline recovery rises to 42-55%. Aperture and flux-calibration uncertainties limit absolute line-flux comparisons. Narrow-line excitation, Chandra spectroscopy (intrinsic N_H ~2.3 x 10^23 cm^-2 in the fiducial model), and long-term optical and mid-infrared variability support an absorbed, variable Seyfert nucleus. The model-dependent 2024 broad-H-alpha candidate and limited 2004 sensitivity do not establish a change in broad-line visibility between the epochs.

summary: We study the holographic imprint of polarization in the lowest BPS multiplet of the IKKT matrix model. On the matrix model side, the deformation requires operator mixing and broken-symmetry Ward identities to organize the surviving operators into an irreducible atypical multiplet of the $F(4)$ superalgebra. In the bulk, we use one-dimensional maximal gauged supergravity to identify the analytic half-BPS background with $F(4)$ symmetry whose boundary behavior matches the IKKT polarization. We solve the linearized bosonic and fermionic equations around this background and its undeformed counterpart exactly, and extract the independent asymptotic data. The supersymmetry transformations of these data reproduce the matrix model multiplets, thus establishing a bulk realization of this BPS operator structure.

title: A resolution-based framework for coherent and decoherent jet energy loss in NLO pQCD
summary: We investigate the role of medium resolution and color decoherence in jet energy loss in high-energy heavy-ion collisions. Within an NLO pQCD framework, implemented using NLOJet++, we calculate inclusive jet production in $pp$ collisions and extend the calculation to $AA$ collisions by incorporating nuclear PDFs, Glauber geometry, and medium-induced jet energy loss in the Higher-Twist formalism. To account for the finite resolution of the QGP, we introduce a sequential coherent clustering procedure based on the pairwise invariant mass of final-state partons. The resulting coherent clusters act as independent color sources when resolved by the medium, with the transition governed by an effective resolution scale $Q_{\rm med}$. We validate the coherent clustering procedure using PYTHIA simulations and investigate the nuclear modification factors of inclusive jets, reclustered jets, soft-drop $r_g$, and jet mass in Pb+Pb collisions at $s_{NN}=5.02$ TeV. Comparison with the ATLAS measurements yields $Q_{\rm med}=10-20$ GeV. While coherent energy loss alone systematically underestimates the observed suppression at high jet $p_{\rm T}^{\rm jet}$ and fails to reproduce the substructure dependence of jet quenching, incorporating decoherent energy loss provides a consistent description of these observables. Our results demonstrate that accounting for the medium's ability to resolve jet substructure is essential for a consistent description of jet quenching in heavy-ion collisions at the LHC.

title: A High-Resolution Stellar Extinction Map of M31 from PHAT and PHAST Photometry
comment: 18 pages, 9 figures, accepted by The Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series (ApJS) on 19 November 2026
summary: High-resolution extinction maps of resolved external galaxies, such as M31, are crucial not only for accurately correcting dust extinction and reddening toward individual sources within the galaxy, but also for characterizing the distribution and evolution of interstellar dust in external galactic environments. We aim to construct a high-resolution and large-coverage stellar-traced extinction map of M31, based on multi-band photometric data from the HST PHAT and PHAST surveys. Using a stellar template library built from the PARSEC stellar evolution models and adopting the average extinction law of M31, we apply a matching method analogous to the SPar algorithm to derive A_V values for approximately 65 million stars. The extinction map is then generated using a HEALPix adaptive-resolution scheme. The resulting map covers approximately two-thirds of the star-forming disk of M31, with a maximum spatial resolution of 1.61 arcsec. The median extinction across the map is A_V = 1.24 mag. Comparison with previously published stellar- and dust-emission-based extinction maps shows broadly similar large-scale morphology, while differences remain in the extinction values. The extinction map further reveals fine-scale features such as inter-arm filaments, supernova-driven cavities, and spur-like structures. The map has been publicly released through the NADC platform and is expected to serve as an important observational basis for extinction correction in subsequent astronomical observations and for related M31 scientific studies.

title: BMS Charges from Null Hypersurfaces
summary: We show how the gravitational dynamics, phase space and Noether charges of the BMS group at future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$ can be derived as limits of their analogues on null hypersurfaces at finite distance. The Bondi mass-loss and angular-momentum evolution equations arise as limits of the Raychaudhuri and Damour constraints. The Ashtekar--Streubel (aka Wald--Zoupas) symplectic potential arises as a specific member of a two-parameter family of null-boundary symplectic potentials, corresponding to the Dirichlet (aka canonical) polarization, while the other members differ by field-space exact terms, leading to the same radiative pre-symplectic structure but potentially different BMS fluxes. Deriving the BMS charges requires additional care, since BMS generators extended into the bulk are generally not tangent to the null hypersurfaces. After accounting for this and the associated anomalies, the renormalized canonical charges still contain an additional soft contribution. The prescription of a covariant boundary Lagrangian determines a corner improvement that removes this term and recovers the standard BMS charges.

title: Interplay of elliptical laser polarization and scattering geometry in laser-assisted pair production of doubly charged Higgs bosons in the Higgs Triplet Model
summary: We study the pair production of a doubly charged Higgs boson via $e^{-} e^{+}$ in the presence of a polarized laser field in the Higgs Triplet Model (HTM), mediated by the photon and the $Z$ boson exchange. A unified formulation based on generalized Bessel functions is developed for a monochromatic plane wave with arbitrary ellipticity, encompassing linear, circular, and elliptical polarization states. The numerical analysis shows a strong interplay between laser polarization and scattering geometry, affecting both the characteristic multiphoton domain and the relative strengths of individual harmonic contributions. At a fixed cycle-averaged squared laser potential, the peak ratio normalized to linear polarization exhibits distinct geometry-dependent trends, including a reversal of the polarization hierarchy between different incidence configurations. The dependence on the collision energy and doubly charged Higgs boson mass is also investigated, revealing pronounced kinematic effects on the differential cross section. In contrast, the relative polarization pattern remains similar over a broad mass range. These results provide a unified characterization of polarization and geometrical effects on the multiphoton structure of this process.

title: High-precision proper motions toward the Galactic bulge Baade's window from a decade of DECam observations
comment: 23 pages, 18 figures, 3 tables. Accepted for publication by A&A
summary: A complete characterization of the Galactic bulge stellar populations could offer important clues on the formation and evolution of our Galaxy. However, most bulge fields are hampered by high stellar crowding, strong interstellar extinction, and by heavy contamination from foreground disk stars. We aim to derive proper motions (PMs) towards the Baade's window by using DECam observations, extending kinematic studies of the Galactic bulge below the turn-off to a much larger field of view. We combined three datasets observed with DECam in the $r$-band spanning a ${\sim}$ 10-year baseline. As a pilot study, we only analyzed the field covered by a single detector. We developed an astrometric calibration pipeline that corrects for the DECam tree-ring pattern and residual distortions, tying all positions to the Gaia DR3 reference frame, and used them to derive PMs. We isolated the bulge population through a strict cut in $μ_{\ell^\ast}$, refined with a Gaia DR3 parallax selection. We measured PMs for $48\,239$ stars in the pilot field, with a median uncertainty of $0.65$ mas yr$^{-1}$ at $r_0<18$ mag. Our PMs agree closely with Gaia DR3, and reaches ${\sim}1.5$ magnitudes deeper than Gaia and a comparable depth to VIRAC2 in terms of relative completeness. We found velocity dispersions along Galactic longitude and latitude of $σ_{μ_{\ell^\ast}}=2.76\pm0.03$ mas yr$^{-1}$ and $σ_{μ_b}=2.49\pm0.02$ mas yr$^{-1}$ for the Galactic bulge, consistent with HST studies. We estimated a foreground contamination of ${\sim}14\%$ before any kinematic selection. The cleaned color-magnitude diagram reaches below the main-sequence turnoff, and shows no evidence for a large population younger than ${\sim}4$-$5$ Gyr in this field. Moreover, since the LSST camera shares the same CCD technology as DECam, this work offers a valuable precursor for crowded-field astrometry in the Rubin era.

title: The Kerr Metric in Canonical Harmonic Coordinates to All Orders
comment: 36 pages. Codes available at Github https://github.com/pierrevanhove/kerr-metric-harmonic and Zenodo https://zenodo.org/records/24397114
summary: We give in closed form the transformation from Boyer--Lindquist coordinates to the canonical harmonic coordinates of the Kerr metric, to all orders in Newton's constant and in the spin. This is the canonical harmonic chart selected by the MPM prescription and by the harmonic-gauge Einstein recursion sourced by the Kerr multipoles, with the residual homogeneous freedom fixed by the boundary conditions. The chart is the real, time-reversal-covariant combination of the two radial harmonic functions underlying the Cook--Scheel coordinates, which differ from it by a definite residual harmonic transformation. The proof rests on a classification of the residual harmonic freedom. Rotational covariance, parity, time reversal and analyticity in the spin allow a decaying homogeneous solution beyond the linear field only in the spatial components at third post-Minkowskian order, with angular degree $\ell=p+2$ at spin order $a^p$. This sector is a pure gauge mode, equivalent to an MPM gauge moment. The exact chart selects the representative in which this third-PM homogeneous mode vanishes; imposing the same condition on the recursion removes the only residual ambiguity and fixes its solution uniquely. As a consequence, the canonical MPM iteration needs no finite-part regularisation and no harmonicity correction at any order. We give the exact gothic metric and the post-Minkowskian coefficients in closed form through fifth order, where an arctangent function first appears at fourth order. We find agreement with recent canonical MPM and amplitude-based results at fourth order, and we verify the construction in exact arithmetic through fifth order and twelfth order in the spin, with code made publicly available.

title: Banana D-modules
summary: We study the holonomic $D$-module whose solutions are generic-mass banana Feynman integrals with complex propagator powers and spacetime dimension. We call this the banana $D$-module. Two properties of the banana $D$-module are studied: its holonomic rank and the irreducibility of the monodromy representation. This is achieved by relating the banana $D$-module to Lauricella $F_{C}$ hypergeometric systems. Further, we expand the generic-mass banana Feynman integral and the associated discontinuity integral in terms of series solutions. Finally, we analyze the Pfaffian system arising from the banana $D$-module and construct an explicit $d\log$ representation in the equal-mass specialization.

title: Mass Spectra and Radiative Decay Widths of \(D_{s0}^{*}(2317)^+\), \(D_{s1}(2460)^+\) and \(D'_{s1}(2536)^+\)
summary:
Inspired by recent experimental reports on the radiative decay \(D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}γ\) and the branching-fraction ratio \(\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}γ]/\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{+}γ]\), we investigate the mass spectra and radiative decay widths of \(D_{s0}^{*}(2317)^+\), \(D_{s1}(2460)^+\) and \(D_{s1}'(2536)^+\). Within the chiral quark model combined with the Gaussian Expansion Method, the mass spectra obtained agree reasonably well with the experimental data.
  Besides, the branching-fraction ratio obtained in this work is \(\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}γ]/\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{+}γ] = 0.57\) and \(Γ(D_{s0}^{*}(2317)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}γ) = 3.80\,\mathrm{keV}\).
  By analyzing our theoretical results against the latest experimental measurements, we conclude that the \(D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\) can be treated as a mixed state of \(1^1P_1\) and \(1^3P_1\), and it may contain both the \(c\bar{s}\) component and the tetraquark component.
  In addition, we also obtain \(Γ(D'_{s1}(2536)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}γ) = 9.14\,\mathrm{keV}\) and \(Γ(D'_{s1}(2536)^{+}\to D_s^{+}γ) = 8.59\,\mathrm{keV}\) by treating \(D'_{s1}(2536)^+\) as a meson state.
  More precise experimental data are required to pin down the internal structure of these states.

title: The relation between DCN/DNC ratios and gas temperature in late-stage massive star-forming regions using Yebes observations
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A, 28 pages, 13 figures
summary: Deuterated molecules probe the physical and chemical evolution of molecular clouds and star-forming regions. Their abundances depend on temperature, density, and evolutionary stage. DCN and DNC are relatively abundant deuterated isomers that probe temperature-dependent deuterium chemistry. Although [HCN]/[HNC] is often thought to increase in warmer gas, the temperature dependence of [DCN]/[DNC] remains less well constrained. To investigate how [DCN]/[DNC] depends on the gas kinetic temperature, we observed the $J$=1-0 transitions of DCN, DNC, H$^{13}$CN, HN$^{13}$C, HC$^{15}$N, and H$^{15}$NC toward 101 late-stage massive star-forming regions using the Yebes 40m telescope. Gas kinetic temperatures were estimated from CH$_3$CCH 5-4, whose rotation temperature is closely related to the kinetic temperature of dense gas. These temperatures were adopted in the column density calculations and in the analysis of temperature-dependent abundance ratios. We find a moderate positive correlation between the abundance ratio [DCN]/[DNC] and kinetic temperature, which is statistically significant and indicates that DCN becomes progressively more abundant relative to DNC in warmer gas. A weak negative correlation with temperature is observed for $D_{\rm frac}({\rm HNC})$, whereas no statistically significant correlation is found for $D_{\rm frac}({\rm HCN})$. The [HCN]/[HNC] ratios show substantial scatter and no statistically significant correlation with temperature, possibly due in part to optical-depth effects in the $^{13}$C isotopologues and the limited sensitivity of the $^{15}$N isotopologue observations. These results suggest that [DCN]/[DNC] may be governed not only by HCN/HNC isomeric chemistry but also by temperature-dependent deuterium fractionation pathways and the chemical evolution of dense gas.

title: Cosmological Correlators with Triple Massive Exchanges
summary: Among all tree-level contributions to the primordial bispectrum, the triple exchange of massive scalars is the most challenging. In this paper we present an analytical formula for this bispectrum in the form of a double series, which allows the three exchanged fields to have different masses and converges throughout the whole physical region. We obtain it by expanding the mixed propagator with the softest momentum, so that the triple exchange becomes a sum of integrals over two mixed propagators. Each of these integrals satisfies a differential equation and is fixed by its value at equal momentum. We further show that the squeezed limit follows directly from this formula and takes a simple and compact form.

title: Flavor-Modulated Neutrino Communication: Channel Model, Modulation Schemes, and Link Budget for Through-Earth Links
summary: We investigate the physical limits of transmitting information through the Earth using neutrinos, modeling the link as a discrete-input, Poisson-output classical channel whose crosstalk is set by the three-flavor evolution operator in a layered, matter-filled Earth. For the maximum-likelihood receiver, we derive closed-form Bhattacharyya and Chernoff error exponents for Poisson counts, accurate to within 0.4\% of the exact Chernoff limit. We examine three modulation schemes: source-flavor keying (SFK), oscillation-phase keying (OPK), and matter-path keying (MPK). For an Earth-diameter link with a neutrino-factory-class source (\(3 \times 10^{13}\) decays/s) and a 200 kt detector, the mean charged-current event rate is \(1.31 \times 10^{-2}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}\), yet the information rate is only \(1.36 \times 10^{-4}\) bit/s for SFK and \(5.2 \times 10^{-6}\) bit/s for OPK. This reduction occurs because at \(E \simeq 25\) GeV the first oscillation maximum nearly fully relabels \(ν_μ\to ν_τ\) (\(T_{μτ} \simeq 0.98\)); SFK relies mainly on a count-based \(e\)-like channel, while OPK suffers from suppressed appearance probabilities. For DUNE and T2HK with horn-polarity keying, assuming \(10^{4}\) unoscillated events per year, rates are \(\sim 10^{-6}\)--\(10^{-7}\) bit/s. The OPK estimate is highly sensitive to the Earth density profile: full tabulated PREM lowers it threefold relative to a three-layer model, and a \(\pm 2\%\) density rescaling changes it by an order of magnitude, whereas SFK varies by less than 10\%. Flavor modulation does not remove the fundamental flux limit; it adds a signaling dimension with constant-intensity operation and directional access, though these do not constitute a cryptographic guarantee

title: Revisiting the Double Cluster in Perseus: Are NGC 869 and NGC 884 a true binary system?
comment: 17 figures, 6 tables. Accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: We perform a comprehensive study of the Double Cluster in Perseus, NGC 869 and NGC 884, to investigate their nature and evolutionary state. By combining new CCD $UBV(RI)_{KC}$ photometry with high-precision astrometry and photometry from \textit{Gaia} DR3, we determine robust astrophysical parameters, including colour excess, distance, and age. Our analysis confirms that both clusters are young, with an age of $12\pm1$ Myr, and share similar photometric distances of $2.29$ kpc. By integrating these observational constraints with completeness-corrected mass estimates and a suite of N-body simulations, we examine the kinematic and phase-space properties of the system. We find that the internal kinematics of NGC 884 exhibit a stronger and more coherent expansion signature than NGC 869. Our dynamical simulations demonstrate a rapid increase in the separation of the pair during the first 100 Myr, exceeding $1$ kpc. These results indicate that the system is not currently gravitationally bound and does not constitute a binary cluster. Instead, the Double Cluster is presently unbound, and the forward integrations predict that its components will continue to diverge under the influence of their relative motion and the Galactic potential.

title: Probing Compressed Dark Sectors at a Muon Collider through Dilepton Signatures and Machine Learning
summary: The inert doublet model (IDM), a minimal extension of the Standard Model (SM), provides a scalar dark matter (DM) candidate that belongs to the additional Higgs doublet. The model faces challenges in achieving the correct relic abundance for compressed spectra and DM masses in the high-mass range. In this work we investigate the prospects of detecting dark matter candidates at future high-energy muon colliders. Focusing on the process $μ^+ μ^- \to AH$ with subsequent decay $A \to H Z^*$ and $Z^* \to \ell^+\ell^-$, we explore the sensitivity of machine learning techniques, specifically Boosted Decision Trees (BDT) and XGBoost, to distinguish the signal from Standard Model backgrounds. We demonstrate that the combination of advanced multivariate analysis with high-luminosity muon collisions enhances the discovery potential for inert scalars in compressed mass spectra scenarios.

title: Predicting HCN, HCO$^{+}$, multi-transition CO, and dust emission of star-forming galaxies
summary: We present an analytical model of a turbulent clumpy star-forming disk that reproduces the spatially resolved observations for 6 molecular lines and 3 continuum bands at 250-700~GHz in the central 30~pc of the Circinus Galaxy. Using the properties of the stellar disk as input, and when matched to the line and continuum emission, the model yields the Toomre $Q$ parameter, mass accretion rate $\dot{M}$, metallicity $Z$, and cosmic ray ionization rate $ζ_{CR}$. These in turn are used to infer the gas properties (surface density, velocity dispersion, and radial velocity) as well as the star formation rate. Our main findings from the model include a low CO-to-H$_2$ conversion factor that varies with radius in the range $α_{\rm CO}=0.5$--1.5 $M_{\odot}$pc$^{-2}/({\rm K\,km\,s}^{-1})$, close to the canonical value for such environments. It shows that CO(3-2) is a poor tracer of the gas mass surface density $Σ_{{\rm H}_2}$ on these small scales, which is better represented by molecules such as HCO$^+$(3-2) with higher critical density. The steep relation between $Σ_{{\rm H}_2}$ and star formation rate surface density $\dotΣ_*$ is typical of compact starburst systems, and the star formation rate (10~$M_{\odot}$kpc$^{-2}$yr$^{-1}$ averaged over the disk) is high enough to drive a wind. Despite this, and in contrast to typical large scale galactic disks, the energy injection rate into the ISM is dominated by gas inflow through the disk rather than the supernova rate. As such, the decreasing inflow rate at smaller radii could be caused by a wind, or indicate a recent increase of the mass inflow from larger scales. We suggest that such variations in the inflow rate could be associated with the nested spiral structures which have been observed in Circinus.

title: Bulk Wilson Loops from $\mathscr{I}$
summary: A Carrollian description of four-dimensional Yang-Mills theory on partially complexified future null infinity was recently proposed by Opreij, Skinner and Wang in arXiv:2604.09771. In this paper, we give a new form of the Carrollian Yang-Mills kinetic action on real future null infinity, and recover the logarithmic two-point function found by arXiv:2604.09771. We then extend the Carrollian description of Yang-Mills beyond scattering amplitudes by studying the expectation value of a null polygonal Wilson loop in Minkowski spacetime. We propose a boundary operator given by the trace of a cyclic product of holomorphic frames on the good cuts associated with the polygon's vertices. At order $g^2$, we show analytically that the boundary calculation reproduces the rational bulk integrand obtained from a self-dual Lagrangian insertion.

title: Saturation effects in two and three jet production processes at LH$μ$C
summary: Motivated by recent proposal of high energy $μ^+$-hadron collider at CERN, LH$μ$C, which could be a natural extension of the LH$e$C at the end of the HL-LHC stage, we have studied expected gluon saturation effects in two and three jet production processes at DIS; these processes are sensitive to the most basic non-perturbative structure parametrizing hadronic content of small-$x$ gluons, the Weizsäcker-Williams (WW) TMD gluon distribution. For the nominal center-of-mass energy of LH$μ$C $\sqrt{s}=5.3$~TeV we have computed a large selection of observables using the ITMD framework in Mote Carlo setting, both for proton and lead target. In the context of future data-driven precise restrictions of the WW TMD gluon distribution, we have computed several azimuthal angle correlations, including the correlations between pairs of jets as well as the outgoing $μ^+$ and jet plane. We have also computed nuclear modification factors, that show a significant suppression, ranging locally between 30%-40%, depending on the observable.

title: Ultra-diffuse Galaxies in the Kilo-Degree Survey: Globular Cluster Systems in Cluster and Field Environments
summary: Ultra-diffuse galaxies (UDGs) are extreme low-surface-brightness systems whose formation pathways remain debated. Globular clusters (GCs) can trace their early assembly, but wide-area studies of UDG GC populations remain scarce. We study GC systems of 545 high-quality UDG candidates identified in the Kilo-Degree Survey (KiDS) with UDGnet, using a dedicated GC-detection pipeline. We identify 24 UDGs with $N_{\rm GC} \geq 3$ (14 associated with groups or clusters and 10 in the field), and use the globular cluster luminosity function to estimate their distances and physical sizes. At fixed luminosity or stellar mass, group- and cluster-associated UDGs tend to have higher GC counts and specific frequencies than field UDGs, although the distributions overlap substantially. Most systems with $S_N \gtrsim 40$ reside in groups or clusters, while field UDGs generally occupy the lower part of the distribution. Group- and cluster-associated UDGs also more often lie near the upper envelope of the $N_{\rm GC}$--$M_\star$ relation. Empirical GC--halo mass relations consequently imply higher halo masses at fixed stellar mass and lower stellar-to-halo mass ratios, although this environmental trend is mild. These findings are consistent with efficient early GC formation followed by suppressed or prematurely quenched field-star formation, suggesting that GC-rich UDGs may represent an extension of the dwarf-galaxy population. The environmental trends may reflect differences in early assembly, quenching, infall, and survival histories rather than a sharp field--cluster dichotomy.

title: Brane Tilings and Polygons with Two Interior Points
summary: We fully classify the brane tilings and the 4d N=1 supersymmetric quiver gauge theories corresponding to toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds whose toric diagrams are convex lattice polygons with two interior lattice points. There are 45 such polygons up to GL(2,Z) transformations and lattice translations: 5 triangles, 19 quadrilaterals, 16 pentagons and 5 hexagons. We identify all 323 toric phases corresponding to these toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds. For every toric phase, we present the brane tiling with its quiver and superpotential, the perfect matching matrix and the F- and D-term charge matrices. For each brane tiling, we study the mesonic moduli space of the corresponding abelian 4d N=1 theory through its Hilbert series and plethystic logarithm, and identify its generators and their leading relations. We also identify the mesonic global symmetry for each brane tiling and determine the superconformal U(1)R charges.

title: Probing grand unification in the dark dimension: proton decay and collider signatures
summary: We study the geometric connection between a stretched grand-unified state, proton decay, and electroweak Kaluza--Klein (KK) resonances in a dark-dimension-inspired interval model. The gravitational length sets the five-dimensional Planck scale, while a shorter gauge interval controls the KK spectrum and the stretched-state mass. We construct normalized fermion and Higgs profiles, diagonalize the neutral-vector sector, and determine its fermionic widths. Proton partial lifetimes are evaluated using a two-operator, SU(5)-inspired effective matching prescription. One-loop four-dimensional MSSM and split-supersymmetric reference running determines electroweak coupling-crossing scales and the residual strong-coupling mismatch. A selected common-threshold benchmark gives a heavy-state mass of $1.137\times10^{16}$ GeV, a reference crossing of $1.139\times10^{16}$ GeV, and a conditional proton partial lifetime of $8.72\times10^{35}$ years. At a micron-scale gravitational length, suppressed baryon-violating matching amplitudes can satisfy proton limits, although the high-scale mass-matching condition selects a distinct region of the scanned geometry. Independently, a $5$ TeV neutral-vector benchmark yields an inclusive leading-order dielectron cross section of $0.183$ fb over $4.5$--$5.5$ TeV at a collider energy of $13.6$ TeV, before detector selection. The analysis provides quantitative effective-model benchmarks and identifies the remaining high-scale matching and experimental tests.

title: Blowing star formation away in AGN Hosts (BAH) - VI. Warm Molecular Outflows Driven by the Low-Luminosity AGN in NGC 3884
summary: We use the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) Mid-Infrared Instrument (MIRI) Medium Resolution Spectrograph (MRS) to investigate the warm molecular and low ionization gas outflows driven by the low-luminosity Active Galactic Nucleus (AGN) in NGC 3884. By decomposing the emission-line profiles into multiple Gaussian components, we detect both ionized and warm molecular outflows, traced by [Ar ii] 6.99 um and H2 0-0 S(5), respectively. The ionized and warm molecular components both extend to similar distances from the nucleus, reaching approximately ~1.2 kpc. In addition to an outflow component, we detect a double narrow emission component in both ionized and molecular lines, clearly observed along the minor axis with similar amplitudes, while their intensity ratio varies systematically along the major axis. Both components exhibit similar line widths and centroid velocity distributions, indicating that they are not associated with outflows, but instead arise from gas in the galaxy disk. We estimate that the outflow injects momentum into the interstellar medium (ISM) at a rate corresponding to ~0.015 percent of the AGN bolometric luminosity, consistent with a radiation-driven origin. Assuming a constant outflow rate, the gas reservoir would be depleted on a timescale of ~26 Myr, potentially suppressing nuclear star formation in the host galaxy.

title: Gravitational Wave Detection via Massive-Particle Interferometry
summary: Gravitational-wave (GW) observations provide a powerful means of testing general relativity and exploring the physics of black holes and the early universe, motivating the development of complementary detection techniques. Here, we propose and theoretically investigate a GW detector based on massive-particle interferometry, in which the signal is encoded in the relative phase accumulated by a quantum particle traversing a closed-loop trajectory and a reference path. We derive the frequency-dependent GW-induced phase response and examine the parameters on which it depends. These parameters provide a means of tuning the detector response over a broad frequency range, motivating the exploration of tabletop detectors for GW signals at frequencies comparable to and below the LIGO band, in the idealized limit. By exploiting the trajectory-dependent gravitationally induced phase, the proposed scheme offers a distinct and potentially complementary approach to GW detection and motivates further investigation of its experimental feasibility and practical sensitivity.

title: Analysis of the triply-charm tetraquark states via the QCD sum rules
summary: In this work, we construct the diquark-antidiquark type local currents to interpolate the triply-charm tetraquark states, and investigate the spectroscopy of the scalar, axialvector and tensor triply-charm tetraquark states via the QCD sum rules comprehensively. As a byproduct, we obtain the masses of four vector triply-charm tetraquark states.

title: WISDOM Project -- XXIX. Catalogue of CO observations of nearby galaxies and the CO Tully-Fisher relation
summary: We present Tully-Fisher relations (TFRs) that use carbon monoxide (CO) as the kinematic tracer and Wide-Field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE) $W1$-band and Two Micron All Sky Survey (2MASS) $K_\text{s}$-band magnitudes as tracers of stellar luminosity. CO data were obtained using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array for the mm-Wave Interferometric Survey of Dark Object Masses (WISDOM) project for a sample of $102$ galaxies located at redshifts $z \lesssim 0.03$, with $81$ detections. The best-fitting reverse $W1$-band and $K_\text{s}$-band CO TFRs are $M_{W1}=(-7.18\pm0.93)\left[\log\left(\frac{W_{50}/\sin i}{\text{km~s}^{-1}}\right)-2.6\right]+(-24.04\pm0.13)$ and $M_{K_\text{s}}=(-5.95\pm0.62)\left[\log\left(\frac{W_{50}/\sin i}{\text{km~s}^{-1}}\right)-2.6\right]+(-24.01\pm0.10)$, respectively, where $W_{50}$ is the velocity width of each integrated CO spectrum at $50\%$ of its maximum, $i$ is the galaxy inclination and $M$ is the galaxy absolute magnitude. Our results are in excellent agreement with those of Tiley et al. (2016b), and together they constitute a robust local benchmark for the CO TFR. We however measure a shallower slope and a smaller zero-point offset compared to the relation of Tully & Pierce (2000). Due to the morphological diversity of our sample, we construct separate late-type and early-type galaxy (ETG) CO TFRs, finding that ETGs are $1.40\pm0.39$~mag fainter at $W1$ band and $0.89\pm0.28$~mag fainter at $K_\text{s}$ band at a given velocity width. We also generate and include a comprehensive catalogue of WISDOM CO data products for use in future molecular gas studies.

title: Agent-guided construction of Feynman integral bases
summary: Finding bases of Feynman integrals whose differential equations are suitable for phenomenology is a remarkably verifiable task. We exploit this to design two \emph{skills} with which Claude Opus~5.5 produces novel results autonomously, working for several days. For a two-loop five-point family (with two masses and 18 elliptic sectors) and a two-loop superfamily for the radiative jet function with a K3 sector, the agent finds bases whose differential equations are free of poles in the dimensional regulator $\varepsilon$ and at most quadratic in it, and takes the jet-function one to $\varepsilon$-factorized form.

title: Zeroing in on BSM at Colliders
summary: Destructive interference between light and heavy dynamics can produce a zero in the amplitude which, for strongly coupled UV completions, lies parametrically below the heavy threshold. We identify under which assumptions this parametrically light zero exists, and when it admits an effective field theory description. We study how absorptive effects and helicity structure affect the existence of the zero and turn it into a dip. When the dip is kinematically accessible, we show how its position, depth, and curvature constrain the UV dynamics. Collider examples illustrate the importance of interference in indirect searches and the information available when the zero is kinematically accessible.

title: Precise Interstellar Extinction Estimates for Nearly Ten Million Stars Based on Multiple Spectroscopic Surveys
comment: Accepted for publication in Research in Astronomy and Astrophysics (RAA). 22 pages, 9 figures, 2 tables
summary: Accurate interstellar extinction estimates are vital for revealing the intrinsic physical properties of stars and the dynamic structure of the Milky Way. Based on multiple optical and near-infrared spectroscopic surveys, including LAMOST, APOGEE, GALAH, GaiaESO, SEGUE, and DESI, we use MLPs and polynomial regressions to calibrate giants and dwarfs separately onto the APOGEE parameter scale, constructing a combined spectroscopic catalog of nearly ten million stars with calibrated stellar atmospheric parameters. This catalog not only provides a robust dataset for our extinction measurements, but also serves as a reference sample for estimating stellar parameters from photometric surveys. Both cross-survey comparisons and external comparisons with high-resolution spectroscopic benchmarks show good agreement in the calibrated parameters. By applying the star-pair method to this extensive sample, we obtain precise extinction estimates. Incorporating distance information, we characterize the spatial distribution of extinction covering over 33,000 square degrees of the sky. Comparisons with existing literature demonstrate that our extinction estimates achieve an exceptional precision of 0.019-0.022 mag. The value-added catalog and open-source Python pipeline for line-of-sight extinction released in this work will provide robust support for future Galactic structure studies and photometric calibrations.

title: Moment bounds and UV reconstruction from curved positivity cones
summary: The fundamental principles of the S-matrix impose positivity bounds on the Wilson coefficients of EFTs, including the SMEFT. These bounds form convex cones that often have curved boundaries when there are degeneracies among the irreducible two-particle low-energy states. Numerical approximations have previously been used to evaluate these curved cones. We develop a moment-based framework to analytically carve out these cones, particularly those associated with anomalous quartic gauge couplings in the SMEFT. The framework also allows us to reverse engineer UV models from the curved boundaries of the positivity cones.

title: A pseudoscalar Higgs boson interfering with toponium: a QCD analysis of $\mathbf{gg\to A\to t\bar t}$ near threshold
summary: The CMS and ATLAS collaborations have observed an excess of $t\bar t$ events near threshold that is consistent with the formation of the pseudoscalar toponium state $η_t$. A pseudoscalar Higgs boson $A$ with a large coupling to top quarks could contribute part of this excess and the presence of the $A$ boson could be concealed. We point out that, if such a state exists with $M_A$ close to $2m_t$, it necessarily interferes with toponium, since both live in the colour--singlet ${}^1S_0$ channel and share the same Coulomb final--state interaction. Using exact leading--order amplitudes, whose relative phase is fixed by unitarity, and Coulomb resummation applied coherently to the QCD background, the $A$ boson signal and their interference, we show that the line shape is controlled by a single complex number $κ$, the ratio of the resonant and non--resonant amplitudes at the peak. Unitarity fixes ${\rm Im}\,κ=-1$ exactly when $A$ decays into top quarks, so that the interference reduces the resonant rate by $2/|κ|^2$ and produces an exact zero of the ${}^1S_0$ amplitude just above $M_A$. The parameter $κ$ does not depend on the $A$ coupling to top quarks and, with the Coulomb--enhanced width we find $|κ|\approx1.5$--$1.7$ for $M_A=350$--$380$ GeV and, hence, the $A$ resonance is completely distorted. For an $A$ boson accounting for 50\% (25\%) of the observed excess, it enhances the toponium peak by about 10 to 70\% (5 to 35\%), and the threshold excess differs strongly from the sum of the toponium and $A$ contributions.

title: Hotter than Little Red Dots: Two Quasars with $T\sim10^4\,\mathrm{K}$ blackbody-like continua at $z\sim4$
comment: 12 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to AAS journal
summary: Gas envelope models of Little Red Dots (LRDs) predict a transition from cool ($T\sim5000\,\mathrm{K}$), gas-enshrouded accretion to an exposed quasar, but observational candidates remain scarce. We identify two blackbody quasars (BBQs), JADES1180 at $z=3.711$ and GTO1215 at $z=4.552$, among 3,553 sources with archival NIRSpec/PRISM spectra. Both show extremely red rest-frame UV ($β_\mathrm{UV}>2.0$) but blue optical continua ($β_\mathrm{opt}<-0.75$), where $f_λ\proptoλ^β$. Their $Λ$-shaped UV-optical continua peak at $λ\approx3000-4000$ Å and are not reproduced by a quasar template reddened with an SMC-like extinction curve. Under the gas envelope interpretation, UV-to-mid-infrared spectral energy distribution fitting indicates $T_\mathrm{env}\approx7600-10300\,\mathrm{K}$ and $L_\mathrm{env}\simeq(3-15)\times10^{45}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$, placing both sources just above the typical LRD ranges in temperature and luminosity. Both BBQs show hot-dust emission with $T_\mathrm{dust}\simeq1400-1550\,\mathrm{K}$ and X-ray emission with $L_\mathrm{2-10\,keV}\simeq(1.3-4.5)\times10^{44}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. The gas absorption is $N_\mathrm{H}<1.5\times10^{23}\,\mathrm{cm^{-2}}$, indicating Compton-thin absorption sightlines. Both also exhibit far-infrared and millimeter detections, suggesting an additional cooler dust component, potentially associated with their host galaxies. These properties are consistent with a transitional phase in which a hotter gaseous envelope partially exposes the central engine.

title: Beyond the Peak: Constraining early dark energy with the damping tail
summary: Early dark energy is commonly characterized by the amplitude and location of its primary energy-injection peak. We show that its post-peak evolution, which we call the \emph{EDE tail}, provides an additional observable probe of the underlying scalar dynamics and can materially affect its ability to alleviate the Hubble tension. We construct a simple phenomenological framework in which distinct regions of a multiscale scalar potential govern the dynamics at different field scales. As a representative realization, we consider a potential that combines axion-like and $α$-attractor-like regimes, thereby allowing the EDE tail to be reshaped through reflection and asymmetric oscillations. Confronting this framework with cosmic microwave background, baryon acoustic oscillation, and supernova observations, we find an improved fit to the high-$\ell$ CMB data together with a higher inferred bestfit $H_0$. Our results show that the EDE tail retains observable information about the underlying scalar potential that is not captured by the conventional peak parameters alone. This provides a complementary route for constructing and observationally distinguishing EDE scenarios, and potentially for further alleviating the Hubble tension.

title: Quark dipole operators in the gradient-flow scheme at NNLO QCD
summary: Conversion factors for the dimension-five QCD operator basis from the $\overline{\textrm{MS}}$ to the gradient-flow scheme are presented through NNLO in the strong coupling. In the CP-even sector, the results are provided for general quark masses and arbitrary flavor content of the operators. Specifically, this concerns the quark CMDM operator and its mixing with lower-dimensional QCD operators. In the massless case, our results immediately apply to the quark chromoelectric dipole operator. As a by-product, we also determine missing entries in the $\overline{\textrm{MS}}$ anomalous dimension matrix of the CMDM operator to NNLO QCD.

title: A TESS Search for Optical Variability in Intermediate-mass Black Hole Candidates
comment: 14 pages, 9 figures, 1 table. Submitted to ApJ
summary: Optical variability of active galactic nuclei (AGNs) probes accretion onto black holes. We study the optical variability of AGNs in the mass range of intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs, $10^{2-6}\,M_\odot$), whose expected variability damping timescales are of order days. We use the high-cadence photometry of the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) to search for optical variability within its individual 28-day sectors. By applying the Quaver light-curve reduction pipeline and designing artifact-aware variability metrics, we identify 3 sources with high-confidence variability and 17 sources with medium-confidence variability. Fitting damped random walk (DRW) models reveals a tentative timescale-mass correlation in a small, metric-selected subset, but not in the full sample. ZTF difference-image aperture photometry reveals long-term fractional variability of 1.8-7.4% in the high-confidence sources, while most medium-confidence sources have variability below 1%. This study demonstrates that the dense cadence and repeated full-sky observations of TESS are valuable for detecting IMBH optical variability, while also being limited by its instrumental artifacts and relatively shallow field.

title: Dark Energy Based on Modified Gravity: Where the Future Lies?
summary: Based on current observational data, there is a strong possibility that dark energy was in a phantom regime in the near past, and a transition from a phantom to a quintessential regime may have occurred. Since then, many scenarios compatible with the DESI data have been proposed. In particular, there exist several realistic models in the framework of $F(R)$ gravity. In this paper, we show that such realistic models of $F(R)$ gravity may produce an anti-gravity or ghost graviton in the future. The problem could be avoided by further changing the parameters and fine-tuning the initial conditions, but we propose to introduce a potential barrier of the scalar field for the small scalar curvature region, which prevents the Universe from evolving into the anti-gravity or having a ghost graviton region, without the fine-tuning of the initial conditions. We also discuss how this regime can be tested using peculiar velocity and kSZ effect probes.

title: Challenging the Körner-Pati-Woo Theorem in Charmed Baryon Decays
summary: The Körner-Pati-Woo (KPW) theorem is a long-standing selection rule widely used in heavy-baryon decays. In this work, we argue that the conventional valence-color argument underlying the KPW theorem does not, by itself, establish an exact selection rule. The $\rm KPW$-$\rm SU(3)_F$ prediction for $\mathcal{B}(Ξ_c^0\to pK^-)$, inferred from $Λ_c^+\to Ξ^0K^+$, is $17.2\pm6.0$ times the measured value. A joint likelihood fit to five observables in $Ξ_c^0\to pK^-$ and $Λ_c^+\to Ξ^0K^+$ yields a $6.3σ$ discrepancy under the $\rm KPW$-$\rm SU(3)_F$ ansatz. A comparison of $α(Λ_c^+\to Δ^{++}K^-)$ and $α(Λ_c^+\to Σ^{*}π)$ reveals a pronounced sign-sensitive tension. Accommodating these measurements within the KPW constraint requires anomalously large $\rm SU(3)_F$ breaking effects. Future measurements of $Λ^+_c\toΣ^{(*)0}K^+$, $Σ^{(*)+}K^0_S$, $Δ^+η^{(\prime)}$, $Δ^{++}π^-$, $Δ^+π^0$, $Δ^0π^+$, $Δ^{++}K^-$, and $Δ^{+}K^0_S$ would provide high-precision tests of the KPW theorem.

title: An early interaction between the Sagittarius dwarf and the Milky Way I: Fossil signatures in the phase-space structure of the disc
comment: 14 pages, 8 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to MNRAS
summary: Several independent lines of evidence point to an early encounter between the Milky Way and the Sagittarius dwarf galaxy $5$-$7$ Gyr ago. We present four controlled $N$-body+hydro simulations, one of an isolated host galaxy and three of a single interaction between a Milky-Way-like host and a Sagittarius-like satellite on an unbound polar orbit. Relative to the fiducial satellite (with total mass $0.7\times10^{11}$ M$_\odot$), one run increases the satellite's mass by a factor of $1.5$ and another its crossing speed by a factor of $1.4$, giving pericentric speeds of $466$-$634$ km s$^{-1}$ at pericentric radii of $R\simeq15$-$18$ kpc. Comparing the present-day, phase-space structure in radial bins by age of newly-formed thin-disc stars across the runs, we find that stars that existed at the time of the passage are thickened by up to $\sim37$ per cent in mass-enclosed height and heated by up to $\sim5$ km s$^{-1}$ in vertical velocity dispersion relative to the control, while stars formed after the passage are unaffected. The heating signature is also evident when comparing the age-vertical velocity dispersion relation against a heating relation with a power law of $0.38$, obtained by fitting the isolated host. A single, disc crossing from an early interaction thus suffices to leave lasting, datable fossils in the age-resolved vertical structure of a galactic disc. The fiducial run's dispersion jump of $\sim4$ km s$^{-1}$ matches best with that observed in the outer low-$α$ disc of the Milky Way (Das et al. 2024), corresponding to a perturber mass of $0.7\times10^{11}$ M$_\odot$, with a velocity of $466$ km s$^{-1}$ at a pericentric radius of $16.7$ kpc, though the inversion from jump amplitude to perturber mass is good only to a factor of $\sim1.5$.

title: A covariant analysis of massless Dirac fields in LRS spacetimes
summary: We investigate the massless Dirac field in locally rotationally symmetric (LRS) spacetimes using a covariant spinorial-fluid representation, with the spinor current and spin direction aligned with the LRS frame. When the current has both vorticity and sheet twist, characterized by a constant ratio $λ$, the LRS integrability condition relates evolution and propagation derivatives, reducing the field equations to an ordinary differential system that can be integrated exactly. The integrability of the chiral angle forces the heat flux to vanish and the source to saturate the null energy condition along the two radial null directions. A constant boost in the radial Lorentzian two-plane maps the spinor current to a canonical congruence, which is stationary (LRS~I) for $|λ|>1$ and irrotational and geodesic (LRS~III) for $|λ|<1$. In this frame, the local metric is reconstructed in the Goode--Wainwright--Van den Bergh canonical form. For $|λ|>1$ the energy density is positive, and the metric is locally isometric to the horizonless charged Taub--NUT (Brill) metric: in the polar representation, the massless Dirac field supplies a stress--energy tensor algebraically identical to that of the Brill electromagnetic field, with no Maxwell field present. For $|λ|<1$, the energy density is negative and the metric is the hyperbolic ($k=-1$) charged NUT metric with a formal negative squared-charge parameter, whose homogeneous slices are of LRS Bianchi type~VIII.

title: Balancing heavy flavour: Quantum number compensation in the hadronisation of charm and beauty particles in proton-proton collisions
summary:
The hadronisation of heavy quarks remains one of the least understood processes of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD). While the production of heavy quark pairs can be calculated perturbatively in QCD, the subsequent formation of hadrons involves non-perturbative processes. The description of these processes is predominantly model dependent and sensitive to the underlying mechanisms of colour reconnection and string fragmentation. In particular, the conservation of flavour, baryon number and charge imposes constraints on how heavy-flavour hadrons are formed and balanced within the final state.
  In this work, we study how the quantum numbers associated with charm and beauty production are balanced in proton-proton collisions, using events simulated with the PYTHIA-8 event generator. Starting from perturbatively produced ($c\overline{c}$) and ($b\overline{b}$) pairs, we examine how the formation of heavy-flavour mesons and baryons, including $D^0$, $B^+$, $Λ_c^+$, and $Λ_b^0$, is accompanied by compensating particles elsewhere. The analysis focuses on correlations between the identified heavy hadron and the hadronic system responsible for balancing its conserved quantum numbers. We compare three hadronisation configurations that are implemented in PYTHIA: the Monash tune, colour-reconnection models incorporating string junctions (SJ), and close-packing (CP) approaches. We find that the SJ and CP tunes show a substantially enhanced contribution of baryons to the charm and beauty balancing yields compared with the Monash tune; this enhancement becomes more pronounced in high-multiplicity events.
  This study introduces a framework for characterising quantum-number compensation in heavy-flavour production and provides a new way to test hadronisation dynamics using identified charm- and beauty-hadron correlations, which can be explored at current and future collider experiments.

title: Nearly pristine gas and hard ionizing radiation one billion years after the Big Bang
summary: The first stars formed out of light elements (H, He, and Li leftover from Big Bang Nucleosynthesis) and began the chemical enrichment of the Universe. Identifying this first-generation population of stars, known as Population III, and understanding their properties is one of the most ambitious goals of modern extragalactic astrophysics. We report the detection of He and H emission lines and extremely low Oxygen abundance in AMORE6, a strongly magnified galaxy at redshift z = 5.725, i.e. approximately one billion years after the Big Bang, with deep James Webb Space Telescope spectroscopy. He II lambda1640 and lambda4686 emission lines are detected at 16.7 sigma and 4.0 sigma significance, respectively. The observed He II-to-Hbeta ratios are consistent with predictions for extreme ionizing radiation fields and the low chemical compositions typical of Population III stars. Oxygen abundance of the interstellar medium is estimated to be 8 x 10^-4 solar from weak [OIII]lambda4363 and lambda5008 lines, consistent with an almost pristine environment, perhaps enriched by the Pop III stars themselves. Although we cannot exclude alternative sources of hard ionizing radiation, such as accreting black holes, these observations offer the first view of the extremely low metallicity environment where the Universe's first stars are predicted to be born. The data show that such pockets of pristine gas still exist one billion years after the Big Bang and that they are dominated by very massive stars.

title: Numerical tests of 5D APS $η$-invariant phases for 4D chiral fermions
summary: We calculate the phase of a 4D chiral fermion determinant from the 5D Atiyah--Patodi--Singer (APS) $η$-invariant. We study the anomaly-free $SU(5)$ representation $\mathbf{10}\oplus\overline{\mathbf 5}$ on a four-torus, using gauge fields independent of one coordinate. For these backgrounds, the 4D phase can be calculated independently from a 3D Dirac spectrum. For an Abelian background embedded in $SU(5)$, two different 5D bulk extensions reproduce the 4D phase within $0.03\%$ in the tested heat-kernel extrapolations. One extension changes the spatial gauge field along the fifth direction and requires a coupled 5D spectral calculation. An independent single-charge check reproduces the Chern--Simons anomaly coefficient within $0.3\%$ using quadratic extrapolations. We also calculate 5D APS phases for non-Abelian backgrounds in the $SU(4)\times U(1)$ subgroup. For a background generating the full $\mathfrak{su}(4)$ algebra, the 5D phase with a fixed spatial field agrees with the independent 4D phase within $0.5\%$ over the six heat-kernel parameters examined. We further study a varying-field 5D extension for an embedded $SU(2)$ background. These results show that the 5D APS calculation reproduces a nonzero chiral phase after anomaly cancellation.

title: Quantifying the TKM-IKT ambiguity: translating the theoretical benchmark into experimental discriminants for future colliders
summary: This paper, the second of two companion works, translates the theoretical benchmark established in into quantitative predictions for high-energy $γγ$ interactions. We simultaneously confront the TKM and IKT dipole cross-section prescriptions across five representative saturation models (GBW, IIMS, rcBK, AGBS, WYKWC). Evaluating real and virtual cross sections, $F_2^γ$, and heavy-quark production, we demonstrate that the TKM--IKT discrepancy is an irreducible structural ambiguity reaching $48\pm12\%$ at LEP energies and expanding into the TeV regime. We propose three experimental discriminants for future colliders (ILC, CLIC, FCC-ee) --- emphasizing exclusive $γγ\to J/ψ+ J/ψ$ production where quadratic amplitude scaling ($[\mathcal{N}]^2$) magnifies the divergence --- elevating these comparisons from parameter choices to rigorous falsification tests of the foundational premises. Finally, an analytical universality test using GBW DIS parameters establishes the quantitative baseline required to falsify the underlying dipole--target analogy.

title: Baryon-Enhanced Strong Lensing Signatures of Self-Interacting Dark Matter Subhalos
comment: 15 pages, 9 figures. Model code publicly available at https://github.com/MeiwenYang/BaryonicPSIDM
summary: Self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) is generally expected to suppress subhalo strong lensing through core formation, with subsequent gravothermal collapse potentially enhancing it. We show that compact stars can make a viable population of galaxy-hosting SIDM subhalos more efficient lenses than their cold dark matter (CDM) counterparts. When the baryonic potential weakens or reverses the inner velocity-dispersion gradient, SIDM halos suppress or bypass core formation, allowing inner densities to grow from early times. The evolved SIDM subhalos produce larger deflection angles and tangential caustics than in CDM. Such galaxy-hosting subhalos also dominate the galaxy-galaxy strong-lensing (GGSL) budget in clusters, yet lie far below the resolution of cosmological simulations. We calibrate a baryonic parametric SIDM model to predict their effects in the three most massive TNG300-1 clusters, finding GGSL cross sections 1.4--2.7 times those in CDM, comparable to the excess inferred in recent analyses. Baryon-enhanced SIDM lensing can thus account for the observed GGSL excess and predicts stronger perturbations from luminous satellites, testable through resolved distortions of background arcs and rings.

title: Probing grand unification in the dark dimension: proton decay and collider signatures
summary: We study the geometric connection between a stretched grand-unified state, proton decay, and electroweak Kaluza--Klein (KK) resonances in a dark-dimension-inspired interval model. The gravitational length sets the five-dimensional Planck scale, while a shorter gauge interval controls the KK spectrum and the stretched-state mass. We construct normalized fermion and Higgs profiles, diagonalize the neutral-vector sector, and determine its fermionic widths. Proton partial lifetimes are evaluated using a two-operator, SU(5)-inspired effective matching prescription. One-loop four-dimensional MSSM and split-supersymmetric reference running determines electroweak coupling-crossing scales and the residual strong-coupling mismatch. A selected common-threshold benchmark gives a heavy-state mass of $1.137\times10^{16}$ GeV, a reference crossing of $1.139\times10^{16}$ GeV, and a conditional proton partial lifetime of $8.72\times10^{35}$ years. At a micron-scale gravitational length, suppressed baryon-violating matching amplitudes can satisfy proton limits, although the high-scale mass-matching condition selects a distinct region of the scanned geometry. Independently, a $5$ TeV neutral-vector benchmark yields an inclusive leading-order dielectron cross section of $0.183$ fb over $4.5$--$5.5$ TeV at a collider energy of $13.6$ TeV, before detector selection. The analysis provides quantitative effective-model benchmarks and identifies the remaining high-scale matching and experimental tests.

title: Soft-photon resummation for low-energy $e^+e^-$ colliders
summary: We present resummed predictions for $e^+e^- \to μ^+μ^-(γ)$ and $π^+π^-(γ)$ in the multi-photon soft limit, matched to exact NLO. The resummation is performed within the Yennie-Frautschi-Suura framework at the amplitude level. The initial and final-state contributions are included coherently, and NLO accuracy with finite electron, muon and pion masses is achieved. We present our calculation, its implementation in a fast Fortran Monte Carlo integrator, and compare our predictions with the generators BabaYaga, KKMC, Phokhara and McMule, in scenarios inspired by the energy-scan (CMD) and radiative-return (KLOE, BES III, B factories) experiments. We find agreement with BabaYaga, which includes higher-order corrections through a parton shower, at the per-mille level in the cross-sections, and differences of up to two percent with the soft-photon resummation of KKMC. This work represents an important step towards the validation of Monte Carlo generators for low-energy experiments, and will be released in the upcoming new version of Phokhara.

title: Effective theory of quantum black holes with Kretschmann scalar
comment: 12 pages, 15 figures, under review in European Physical Journal C
summary: We investigate the thermodynamics, quasinormal modes (QNMs), and shadows of the effective theory of quantum black holes (BHs) by expanding the physical constants in terms of the Kretschmann scalar. The resulting effective metric can contain two horizons, which is typical for a quantum-corrected Schwarzschild spacetime. The second-order corrected metric only shifts the first-order corrected metric, allowing investigation of IR phenomena from the pure first-order corrected one. From a thermodynamic point of view, the metric leads to a stable cold remnant with zero entropy, compatible with the third law of thermodynamics. In the perturbation regime, we use massless scalar perturbations to extract the effective potential, QNMs, graybody factor, and total absorption cross section. We show that double-horizon BHs have a double light ring in the potential, and for a certain value $Ω/χ^2=0.01,$ the QNMs are similar to the GR case since the horizon is Schwarzschild-like. We also tested the correspondence between the QNMs and the graybody factor, and our results still hold with an error far below $1\%$. Our results also conclude that the higher the frequency, the bigger the cross-section area. For the optical observables, we observe that the opposite sign of $Ω$ leads to distinct behavior of the BH's photon sphere and shadow radius. The Sagittarius A* shadow radius upper bound from the Event Horizon Telescope observation in the $2σ$ and $1σ$ significance set the upper limit of the quantum parameter $Ω$ to $Ω/χ^2 \lesssim 0.3649$ and $Ω/χ^2 \lesssim 0.0105$, respectively.

title: Probing CP violation in weak radiative and dielectron decays of $Λ$ and $Ξ^-$ hyperons
summary: The rare decays $Λ\to ne^+e^-$ and $Ξ^-\toΣ^-e^+e^-$ can serve as sensitive probes of $CP$ violation, especially that induced by interactions from beyond the standard model. We demonstrate that this is so because the dominant long-distance components of these processes provide sizable absorptive phases that can give rise to significant $CP$ violation via interference with potential new-physics effects. Treating the new contributions model-independently, we find that this leads to $CP$-odd rate asymmetries that are currently allowed by kaon and hyperon data to reach the 10% and 20% levels in the $Λ$ and $Ξ^-$ cases, respectively. Interestingly, we obtain comparable outcomes for the related weak radiative modes $Λ\to nγ$ and $Ξ^-\toΣ^-γ$. These results are testable at future high-statistics hyperon facilities.

title: Solving fermionic sign problems with physics-informed kernels
summary: We extend the generative sampling approach with physics-informed kernels (PIKs) [1,2] to a general class of physics systems with complex distributions and a structure also encountered in fermionic systems. The resolution of sign problems of generic weighted sums of complex Gaußian distributions with the PIK approach is central to this application. In a first step, PIKs map a real normal distribution to such a weighted sum, and this procedure is called the PIKfan. The PIKfan has the sampling cost of a real normal distribution. In a second step, this weighted sum is evolved with a second PIK into the distribution of the theory at hand. In combination, we reduce the sampling task for a general class of complex systems to a Gaußian one, and the main computational task is that of computing the PIK. We illustrate the approach with the one-site Hubbard model at arbitrary chemical potential and with $φ^4$-deformed extensions of it.

title: Is Neutrino Disappearance Sensitive to T-Violation for Asymmetric Matter Profiles ?
summary:
It is commonly stated in the literature that T violation is zero in neutrino disappearance channels. We show this claim is not general: it holds only for symmetric matter profiles or when the T/CP-violating phase ($δ$) is 0 or $π$, that is, when the Jarlskog invariant is zero. The $ν_μ$ and $ν_τ$, but not the $ν_e$, survival probabilities carry a $\sinδ$-dependent term that is non-zero in asymmetric matter and constitutes a genuine T asymmetry. The confusion arises from an improper T test that subtracts a probability from itself: a mathematical identity, not a physics result. In this paper, we clarify the distinctions between a proper and an improper T test as well as the proper and improper CP and CPT tests, for a general, arbitrary matter profile.
  For a toy model consisting of two different layers of constant density, we find that the maximum T-violation is obtained when one layer is close to the solar resonance, and the other is close to the atmospheric resonance. We address whether the matter asymmetry for DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokande experiments is sufficiently large to allow the $\sinδ$ dependence to be probed in $ν_μ$ survival probability. We also discuss future experimental scenarios that could probe T/CP-violation in $ν_μ$ survival probability.

title: Ohmic warm inflation
summary: We show that Warm Little Inflation is anomalous, lacks a suitable inflaton potential, and cannot sustain the thermal bath, as the quasi-static approximation over-estimated the dissipated power. To address these issues, we propose a new friction mechanism and new anomaly-free models based on one fermion charged under a U(1) gauge group in one extra dimension. The four-dimensional lattice version is a ring of $N$ U(1) groups with one fermion at each site, reducing to an anomaly-free version of the warm little inflaton model for $N=2$. The inflaton is a Wilson line, protected for $N\ge5$. Large $N$ allows a suitable monodromy inflaton potential. In the continuum limit, $N\to\infty$, the inflaton velocity becomes a five-dimensional electric field and friction becomes Ohmic dissipation, which seems able to sustain warm inflation compatibly with observations.

title: Features investigated: A detailed study of axion monodromy inflation using CLiENT
summary: We investigate features in the primordial power spectrum from inflation, specifically those predicted by the axion monodromy model, using recent observational data. In order to compute posteriors, profile likelihoods and Bayesian evidence accurately for the complex likelihood surfaces arising in this model we have used the CLiENT emulator framework. As our data combinations we use both a "conservative" set consisting of Planck PR4 temperature, polarisation and lensing data together with DESI DR2 BAO and Pantheon+ supernovae, and a more "aggressive" set which also includes small-scale CMB data from ACT and SPT. We find no robust oscillatory feature in current data. With the conservative data the best fit lies at a frequency $ω\simeq 51$ and lowers $χ^2$ by 10.1 relative to a featureless spectrum. However, this feature is disfavoured by the more aggressive data combination, whose best fit lies at $ω\simeq 31$ and lowers $χ^2$ by 7.4. Fits to featureless data are known to give similar improvements, and the Akaike information criterion, the Bayes factors and the look-elsewhere effect all indicate that neither improvement is significant. The amplitude is limited to $A_\mathrm{osc} < 0.056$ and $A_\mathrm{osc} < 0.062$ (95%) for the two datasets. The emulators reproduce the true log-likelihood at samples of their posteriors with rms errors of 0.07 and 0.16, and the profile likelihoods are calculated with the true likelihood, using the profile capability of CLiENT.

title: Regularizing gravity in the presence of matter fields
summary: We investigate how matter fields affect spacetime regularity in a class of gravitational theories with second-order field equations in spherical symmetry, of which general relativity is a special case, and which may encode effective corrections from an underlying quantum theory of gravity. Focusing on spherically symmetric black holes and cosmological spacetimes in theories in which vacuum spacetimes display bounded curvature invariants, we derive the conditions under which regular geometries can be supported by static and perturbative scalar fields, electromagnetic fields, and radiation fluids. We discuss the impact of matter on the regularity requirements of curvature boundedness and geodesic completeness relative to vacuum, finding in general that coupling to matter does not eliminate the existence of theories with regular solutions.

title: Cosmological Correlators with Triple Massive Exchanges
summary: Among all tree-level contributions to the primordial bispectrum, the triple exchange of massive scalars is the most challenging. In this paper we present an analytical formula for this bispectrum in the form of a double series, which allows the three exchanged fields to have different masses and converges throughout the whole physical region. We obtain it by expanding the mixed propagator with the softest momentum, so that the triple exchange becomes a sum of integrals over two mixed propagators. Each of these integrals satisfies a differential equation and is fixed by its value at equal momentum. We further show that the squeezed limit follows directly from this formula and takes a simple and compact form.
